item554.reading: Printed glyph looks like ר (יוֹרוּ). Intended word is יוֹדוּ. If a human confirms, encode as <sic>יוֹרוּ</sic>/<corr>יוֹדוּ</corr>.
item554.decision: I read the second letter as ר, not ד. I am not treating it as unresolved, but I am not confirming it either: at this resolution a resh sort and a dalet whose corner has broken off or failed to ink look alike. The working text still has יוֹדוּ unchanged. I have not silently corrected it to resh or to dalet. Applying sic/corr needs a human decision.
evidence: snippets/554.png: the top-right corner of letter 2 in יורו is rounded. The roof runs into the right leg in a curve and nothing sticks out to the right of the leg. Earlier passes saw the same thing.

Same snippet, וִיאַדְּרוּךָ (the same small typeface, a few words to the left): its ד has a square corner with the roof sticking out past the leg. Its ר is rounded. Letter 2 of יורו matches that ר, not that ד.

detail1-right, L4 יוֹדֽוּךָ (large type) and L5 יוֹדֽוּךָ (small type, same size as L3): both ד have the square corner with the roof sticking out. The L5 ד is the most direct comparison because it is in the same type size as L3, and letter 2 of L3 does not match it.
detail1-right, L6 עֲבָדֶֽיךָ: the ד has the square corner with the roof sticking out.
detail1-right, L4 וְיָרִיעוּ: the ר is rounded with no overhang. It matches letter 2 of L3.
detail1-right, L1 כָּרָאוּי (small type): the ר is rounded with no overhang. It matches letter 2 of L3.
full-329.png, line 3: shows the same thing at lower resolution. Letter 2 of the first word looks like the ר elsewhere on the page, not the ד.
There is no ink trace or gap where a dalet's overhang would be, as far as the JPEG shows. The JPEG cannot show whether a damaged dalet sort was used.
item554.translation_support: Salaman stanza 57, 'The heavens shall acknowledge your wonders', supports dalet (יודו) as the intended wording. So does the parallelism with יוֹדֽוּךָ in L4 and L5. The line also seems to echo Ps 89:6, וְיוֹדוּ שָׁמַיִם פִּלְאֲךָ. I am citing that from memory and have not checked it against a text. All of this supports a <corr> of יוֹדוּ. None of it is evidence about which glyph is printed, and I did not use it to override what the image shows. יוֹרוּ ('they shall teach') reads poorly in context, which fits a misprint.

remaining_reading_disputes.question: In both the full page and the crop the vowels look like segol under the א and qamats under the ח, which would be לְאֶחָי, the form in Ps 22:23 אֲסַפְּרָה שִׁמְךָ לְאֶחָי. The working text has לְאַחַי, with patah under both. Earlier passes did not raise this. Is it לְאֶחָי or לְאַחַי?

limitations: Item 554: the JPEG cannot tell a resh sort from a dalet with a broken or poorly inked corner. My ר reading describes how the glyph looks. It does not establish what sort the typesetter used.
פָּעַל (Monday L13, after מַה): a dot seems to be inside the pe, but it is too small to confirm the dagesh. The working text is not contradicted. No human ruling covers it.
I can only rule out metegs as far as the image shows them. I raised words as disputes only where I saw a possible mark. Other words with no visible mark are left as the working text has them.
notes: I checked every human ruling 552–569 against the working text for page 329, and each one is applied only where it was ruled. 552 קָדְשֶֽׁךָ is exact and the wrong ת is gone. 553 has qamats under the resh. 555 הַשָּׁמָֽיִם has qamats and meteg under the mem. 556 יְהַלֲלוּ has the hataf patah. 557–560 are applied, and 560 is in L4. 561 בֶּן and 561 אֲמָתֶֽךָ / גְּבוּרוֹתֶֽיךָ are applied. 562 and 569 נּוֹרָא keep the dagesh, and both מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ are applied. 563 חֵֽקֶר is applied. 564 אֵלֶֽיךָ has the meteg and אַגִּידָה has no meteg on the gimel. 565 כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ is exact. 566–568 are applied, including שַֽׂמְתִּי with the sin dot. No כבודך change was inferred for 561, and 554 is still יוֹדוּ. None of these were reopened.
The earlier correction יָדָע→יֵדָע (Monday L8) is already in the working text.

The horizontal strokes just before the word in ־עַל (Sunday L1, Monday L17), ־עֲרוֹךְ (L3), ־עַיִן (L7) and ־יַעֲקֹב (L6) look like the patah or hataf patah under the ayin, set off to the right as this typeface does. They are not metegs or maqafs. In s329 L7 עַיִן I see no vertical meteg stroke, so I did not raise it, even though the s328 parallel has עַֽיִן.
